item.title: CVE-2026-126777 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 9.1
item.description: Wednesday 11 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 9.1 | Traccar 3.15 before 6.17.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in LdapProvider.login() that fails to reject empty passwords, causing LDAP binds to be performed as unauthenticated binds when LDAP authentication is enabled. item.title: CVE-2026-58505 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Wednesday 11 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | geojson-vt is a JavaScript library for slicing GeoJSON data into vector tiles on the fly, primarily designed to enable rendering and interacting with large geospatial datasets on the browser side (without a server). Prior to version 6.1.1, @maplibre/geojson-vt contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in its GeoJSON conversion logic. When a GeoJSONVT instance is constructed with a deeply nested GeometryCollection object, the mutually recursive functions featureToInternal and convertGeometryCollection in src/convert.ts exhaust the Node.js call stack, causing an unhandled RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded that terminates the process. Because the library is widely used in server-side tile services that accept GeoJSON over the network, a remote unauthenticated attacker can trigger a denial-of-service by sending a single crafted payload. No authentication is required, and no non-default library options are needed. This issue has been patched in version 6.1.1.

item.title: CVE-2026-63505 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 4.9
item.description: Wednesday 11 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 4.9 | Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.223.1, Probo's console GraphQL API is a multi-tenant GRC platform where all data is scoped to an organization. A Finding can reference a Risk via finding.riskId. That reference is stored without validating that the risk belongs to the caller's organization, and the Finding.risk field resolver authorizes the finding (caller's org) instead of the risk, then loads the risk with a tenant scope derived from the risk's own global ID. As a result, an authenticated member of organization A can attach an arbitrary organization B risk GID to a finding they own and then read organization B's Risk (name, description, treatment, category, severity, owner) — with no membership in B. The stored cross-tenant reference also blocks B from deleting its own risk (ON DELETE RESTRICT), a cross-tenant integrity/DoS. This issue has been patched in version 0.223.1.

item.title: CVE-2026-76078 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 3.1
item.description: Wednesday 11 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 3.1 | Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.224.0, the public Trust Center GraphQL API exposes acceptElectronicSignature and recordSigningEvent, both gated only by @authentication(required: PRESENT) @sessionOnly — any self-provisioned trust center identity can call them. The underlying esign.Service.AcceptSignature and esign.Service.recordEvent build the tenant scope from the client-supplied signatureId GID (coredata.NewScopeFromObjectID(req.SignatureID)) and load the signature by that GID. At no point do they verify that the signature belongs to the caller or that the caller's email matches the signature's SignerEmail. As a result, any authenticated trust-center visitor who possesses another visitor's signature GID can: (1) complete that visitor's NDA signature — overwriting signer name/IP/UA with attacker data and setting status to Accepted, which triggers the sealing worker to generate a completion certificate; (2) inject arbitrary audit-trail events into any signature's log. Both attacks defeat the non-repudiation and integrity guarantees of the e-signature system. This issue has been patched in version 0.224.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-76080 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 3.7
item.description: Wednesday 11 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 3.7 | Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.224.0, the public Trust Center GraphQL API exposes Query.node(id:) with @authentication(required: OPTIONAL) — an unauthenticated internet visitor to any published trust center can call it. Six of its type branches — Organization, Framework, Audit, ThirdParty (subprocessor), TrustCenter, and TrustCenterReference — resolve the object with a tenant scope derived from the client-supplied GID itself (coredata.NewScopeFromObjectID(id)) and load it with a bare Get(scope, id) that performs no comparison to the current trust center's OrganizationID and no showOnTrustCenter/visibility check. (The Document and File branches, by contrast, correctly pass trustCenter.OrganizationID and check visibility). This issue has been patched in version 0.224.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-91151 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.3
item.description: Wednesday 11 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.3 | A flaw was found in Cockpit. A local authenticated user with control over a target account's home directory can exploit a privileged symlink dereference vulnerability in the `ssh-add-public-key.sh` helper. When this helper runs with elevated privileges, it can be tricked into following attacker-controlled symlinks within the `.ssh` or `authorized_keys` paths. This allows the attacker to arbitrarily change file ownership and modes, potentially leading to local privilege escalation and impacting the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of the system.
